games.title: Reading Detective
games.description: Use unit evidence to solve each reading clue.

rounds.prompt: What did the principal announce about the student records at the board meeting?
choices: He said the records indicate that Form 3 had cleaned more consecutively than the other forms, which disproved the anonymous teacher's accusation.
The school held a hearing and reviewed testimonies, the boy was exonerated, and it turned out that a loose screw, not a student, had caused the damage.
They correct their mistakes publicly, welcome opposition from readers who disagree, and print their reporters' names so that every story has a named author.
rounds.answer: He said the records indicate that Form 3 had cleaned more consecutively than the other forms, which disproved the anonymous teacher's accusation.
rounds.explanation: At the board meeting the principal says, 'the student records indicate that Form 3 cleaned more consecutively than other forms.' That fact answered the anonymous teacher's claim that Form 3 had skipped duty.

rounds.prompt: How do reliable news organisations respond to mistakes and to readers who disagree, according to the passage?
choices: He said the records indicate that Form 3 had cleaned more consecutively than the other forms, which disproved the anonymous teacher's accusation.

They correct their mistakes publicly, welcome opposition from readers who disagree, and print their reporters' names so that every story has a named author.
rounds.answer: They correct their mistakes publicly, welcome opposition from readers who disagree, and print their reporters' names so that every story has a named author.
rounds.explanation: In the paragraph about how serious journalism works, the text says reliable news organisations print their reporters' names, welcome opposition from readers who disagree, and correct their mistakes publicly.

rounds.prompt: How was the accusation about the vandalised locker resolved, and what did the hearing reveal?
choices: He said the records indicate that Form 3 had cleaned more consecutively than the other forms, which disproved the anonymous teacher's accusation.
The school held a hearing and reviewed testimonies, the boy was exonerated, and it turned out that a loose screw, not a student, had caused the damage.
They correct their mistakes publicly, welcome opposition from readers who disagree, and print their reporters' names so that every story has a named author.
rounds.answer: The school held a hearing and reviewed testimonies, the boy was exonerated, and it turned out that a loose screw, not a student, had caused the damage.
rounds.explanation: The text says they held a hearing, testimonies were reviewed and the boy was exonerated, because 'a loose screw had caused the damage'. Zara had insisted, 'You can't punish someone on what's alleged.'
